questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: In general I just love Italy, so Erasmus was a great personal opportunity for living in Italy.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Milan webpage contains a lot of information, but I needed to search for it myself, because I did not receive a lot of information directly from University of Milan.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The assistance there was; was a visit at the international mobility office of University of Milan. I got stamped my proof of attendance, an opportunity to ask questions and a goodiebag. It should be mentioned, that it was not a lot of assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: University of Milan has around 4 different accommodations opportunities located approx. 30-60 minutes away from the center of Milan.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a common kitchen for all of the campus' residences.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is easy and you get the opportunity to meet a lot of people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a very good idea to get accommodation from University of Milan, because it is a lot cheaper than finding accommodation yourself in Milan, but you need to be very outreaching yourself to get the accommodation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I made a study plan on the platform Unimia belonging to the University of Milan.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It is possible to send an email to the international mobility office of the University of Milan.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very succesful and I got exactly the courses I wanted. It is possible to change courses while you are at the exchange and it is possible to attend to courses at another faculty.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it chill, everything is going to be fine, when you are in Milan.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was a little bit lower than the level at Copenhagen University. However still a high level. I took some master courses as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is smaller lectures, where the students participate more and in some classes there are student presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I had the courses; Public Economics, International Economics and Policy, Economic History and Empirical Methods for Inequality Analysis. It should be mentioned, that the University of Milan has a trimester system on the Social Science faculty.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend the course International Economics and Policy. The professor was really encouraging and the course was really interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think there was any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: For me everything was as expected. However I think accommodation can be a more expensive than expected, if it is not possible to get the university accommodation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was Erasmus events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Personally I did not attend to so many Erasmus events, because they began two months later than my arrival to Milan, but I think they can be cool.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend to take a lot of trips in Italy. Milan is located perfect to get to a lot of cool destinations.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and talk with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love the chill vibe in Italy and the food is amazing!!!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You will figure everything out, when you arrive on your Erasmus, so do not stress about practical stuff. 
Also be chill during your courses; information often comes late, but it will come. 
You will have a great time :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The above-mentioned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of personal growth and it was really giving to try to live in another country. Also all of the friends a got from all over Europe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think there was 1 week, where I was stressed by being "alone" in the city, but then suddenly I meet so many nice people and got so many nice friends, so that feeling was fast gone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
